headline: US stocks ended slightly lower as weak retail sales and softer consumer sentiment contrasted with ongoing weekly gains and strength in energy shares
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 (SPY), Dow Jones Industrial Average (DIA), and Nasdaq Composite (QQQ) all closed modestly lower, though the S&P 500 (SPY) still logged a third straight weekly advance
- July retail sales fell 0.6% month-over-month, the largest drop in over a year and well below expectations for a small gain
- The preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment index slipped to 51.0, signaling rising worries about inflation and the economic outlook
- Technology shares led declines, with Broadcom (AVGO) among the weakest performers and Applied Materials (AMAT) sliding around 5% despite beating earnings forecasts as investors sought faster growth
- Energy stocks advanced, supported by rising oil prices
- Small-caps outperformed, with the Russell 2000 (IWM) up about 0.56% and select AI-related and memory names showing relative strength
- SanDisk (SNDK) extended gains after JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight following the company’s Investor Day
- Reddit (RDDT) jumped roughly 13% after being selected to join the S&P 500 (SPY) on August 18, replacing AvalonBay Communities (AVB)
- Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-B) added to its Alphabet (GOOGL) position, disclosed a new D.R. Horton stake and bank trims, and exited its holding in Constellation Brands (STZ)
- In after-hours trading, Workday (WDAY) surged on reports of preliminary buyout talks with Silver Lake, while investors turned attention to upcoming housing data, industrial production, and earnings from Home Depot (HD), Baidu (BIDU), and Toll Brothers (TOL)
